source_text:
Βάπτισμα γὰρ κἀκεῖνο τελευταῖον, οὐ σωτήριον, ἀλλὰ

τῆς μὲν κακίας ἀναιρετικόν· οὐκέτι γὰρ κακία καὶ ἁμαρτία πολιτεύεται· κολάζον δὲ
ἀτελεύτητα.
thought_title: The final baptism destroys evil but punishes endlessly
orientation: John of Damascus is explaining why Christ's baptism with fire can refer to the final punishing fire, and here he describes what that last baptism does.
pass_a_gloss: For that baptism also is final, not saving, but destructive of evil; for no longer does evil and sin hold sway; but the fire punishes endlessly.

choices.why: The adjective modifies βάπτισμα and matches the brief's description of the 'final punishing fire'; 'last' would also work but 'final' better conveys the eschatological sense.
The brief states this baptism is 'not saving but destructive of evil'; 'saving' preserves the adjectival force of σωτήριον.
The brief says the final baptism is 'destructive of evil'; the genitive κακίας is rendered with 'of' to keep the construction clear.
The brief says evil and sin will 'no longer hold sway'; this rendering captures the political/civic metaphor of πολιτεύω as exercising dominion.
The glossary mandates 'endlessly' for ἀτελεύτητα, describing the punishment.
